Egress IP addresses and static NAT
SAML SSO and RBAC for console

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-05 15:30 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording available)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO), Priya (Sr Network Eng), Derek (Compliance), Sam (Platform)

Summary (auto): High-level intake for private/VPC deployment; focused on networking constraints and compliance needs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:00:06] Alex: Hey, Alex Moreno, CTO at Brookhaven. We're trying to scope running Redwood in our VPC rather than public internet, mostly for compliance.
[00:00:12] Priya: Priya Singh, senior network engineer. I'll be owning the VPC bits.
[00:00:16] Derek: Derek, compliance. Looking for auditability and residency guarantees.
[00:00:19] Sam: Sam Wells, platform. I'll help with the POC env.
[00:00:22] Maya: Great. Liam and Rina from our solutions team are here to go into design details. Quick agenda: network topology, egress/IP, private endpoints, region gating — then we'll capture next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:34] Alex: Yep, go for it.
[00:00:37] Liam: Cool. To start, can you run us through your current infra pattern? Are you using multi-account VPCs, transit gateway, or single VPC with peering?
[00:00:45] Priya: We're multi-account, using a transit gateway in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Most of our prod workloads are EU-first for privacy regs, but dev sits in us-east. We want Redwood to live in our EU footprint.
[00:00:58] Rina: When you say "live in EU footprint", you mean the inference plane should be in eu-west-1 and not egress to US, correct?
[00:01:04] Alex: Exactly. No tokens or payloads leaving the EU region.
[00:01:08] Derek: And all audit logs need to be retained for 2 years, and we need to show KMS encryption for any keys.
[00:01:14] Maya: Understood. We support private deployments in customer VPCs in EU regions. Our Private product can be deployed in your VPC via a private control plane and interface endpoints. There are two common patterns — VPC peering to our service VPC, or using a transit gateway with an appliance model.
[00:01:31] Priya: We prefer transit gateway because it's how our networking team manages routing and security controls. Peering becomes messy across dozens of accounts.
[00:01:38] Liam: That makes sense. One caveat — transit gateway has limitations around cross-account firewalling, but we can work with your team on route tables and security groups. We can also deploy a small private edge in your VPC that talks to our control plane over PrivateLink.
[00:01:52] Priya: When you say PrivateLink, is that equivalent to AWS PrivateLink service endpoints? We call them interface endpoints.
[00:01:58] Liam: Yes — interface endpoints (PrivateLink). We expose an endpoint service you can attach. That keeps traffic on the AWS fabric.
[00:02:03] Sam: Do you require any public NAT for model updates or pulls? Our policy is no public egress from EU.
[00:02:09] Rina: We have options. Model artifact sync can happen via an internal S3 mirror. Alternatively, we can stage models into your region; we don't need egress to the public internet for model loads. There was one customer where we did a seeded sync via secure transfer, but that's more for air-gapped scenarios.
[00:02:24] Priya: Good. Also, we'll need a stable egress IP for allowlisting with downstream partners (forwards to payment gateways). Can Redwood guarantee static egress IPs from the inference nodes?
[00:02:33] Liam: We can provide NAT gateways in the VPC under your control, so egress IPs are yours to manage. If you run the inference node in your VPC, egress is from your NAT. If you want Redwood-managed egress, we can allocate stable IPs via a managed NAT, but that requires a contractual arrangement.
[00:02:48] Derek: For compliance, we need proof that no logs or payloads are retained outside the VPC. How does Redwood handle logs and telemetry?
[00:02:55] Maya: We keep control plane logs in our control plane, but you can opt into forwarding audit logs to your SIEM via a secure forwarding endpoint. For Private deployments, all inference payloads are local; only metadata required for billing and telemetry is forwarded with PII redaction. We'll share our SOC2 artifact.
[00:03:12] Derek: Metadata for billing — can that be routed to an EU region as well?
[00:03:15] Rina: Yes, we can configure the control plane to store billing/usage in EU storage backends for your account. We'll need to map the storage endpoints during setup.
[00:03:23] Alex: Latency is a big thing for us — real-time trading features. We're seeing 60–80ms p95 on our in-house models. What's realistic with Redwood in a private VPC in eu-west-1?
[00:03:34] Liam: If inference nodes are colocated in eu-west-1 and traffic is intra-VPC, we've seen p95s around 30–70ms depending on model size and batch policy. For LLMs with short context windows, p50 can be sub-30ms. For large 8k contexts it grows. We should benchmark with your exact prompt profile.
[00:03:52] Priya: For benchmarking, we need a sample traffic mix. Sam will provide that.
[00:03:56] Sam: I'll share our synthetic load — mostly single-turn, ~200 tokens, bursty at market open.
[00:04:02] Liam: Perfect. We'll design a test harness that emulates your burst profile, include KV cache warmup, and measure token/sec and p95 latency.
[00:04:08] Alex: We also have strict key management rules — all keys must be in our KMS and HSM. Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
[00:04:15] Rina: Yes, we support using customer-managed KMS for encrypting model artifacts and any keys. For HSM-backed signing, there are integration patterns — we usually work with your security team to handshake key rotation and access.
[00:04:27] Derek: Ok, and SSO — we use SAML with IdP and want role-based access to models and cost controls.
[00:04:33] Maya: Redwood Console supports SAML SSO and granular RBAC. For Private, the control plane will accept your IdP assertions; we'll map groups to roles. We can supply the SAML metadata once the control plane hostname is provisioned.
[00:04:43] Priya: A practical question: if we provision Private in our VPC, who manages upgrades and kernel changes? We need maintenance windows.
[00:04:49] Liam: We typically do rolling upgrades with scheduled maintenance windows. For Private, we can either run it in a managed mode where Redwood orchestrates upgrades inside your tenancy (with your approval windows), or hand you the helm for on-prem style. Most customers choose managed with an SLA for patching.
[00:05:02] Alex: Cost tradeoff — what's the delta between Dedicated vs Private? We want predictability but also data isolation.
[00:05:08] Maya: Dedicated is Redwood-managed in isolated tenant capacity on our hardware; Private is deployed into your VPC. Dedicated gives easier onboarding but requires data egress agreements for some metadata. Private gives the strictest isolation but higher setup effort and potentially higher ops responsibilities. We'll put a side-by-side in the follow-up pricing sheet.
[00:05:25] Derek: Any competitors we should be aware of? We're seeing BigCloud's managed endpoints pitched, and one vendor called EdgeServe.
[00:05:31] Maya: Noted — we'll include a competitive note.
[00:05:35] Priya: A nit — what's your recommended subnet sizing and IP consumption per inference node? We have limited ENIs per subnet.
[00:05:43] Liam: For our current runtime, each worker requires one primary ENI and potentially a secondary for monitoring interfaces; plan for ~2 IPs per GPU worker. For scaling, we recommend /22 for a typical POC, but we'll size to your expected concurrency.
[00:05:59] Sam: Are there any kernel level or NVLink requirements? Our infra team wants GPU topology details.
[00:06:04] Rina: We can provide a hardware compatibility matrix. For customer-hosted clusters, we support standard NVIDIA stack; we also have quantized runners that are less GPU-memory heavy. We'll share the matrix after the call.
[00:06:16] Alex: For the POC success criteria, p99 < 150ms and >= X tokens/s is our baseline. We'll define exact X after we share traffic.
[00:06:24] Liam: Sounds reasonable. For the POC we'd propose 2 weeks: week 1 for deployment and smoke tests, week 2 for load tests and tuning.
[00:06:31] Priya: Do you have a checklist for our network team so we can pre-approve security groups and route tables?
[00:06:37] Maya: Yes — we'll send a Private deployment network checklist that lists required ports, endpoints, and expected CIDR ranges.
[00:06:43] Derek: On the logs topic again — what granularity of audit logs do you capture? We need per-request audit trails for a sample of requests.
[00:06:51] Rina: We capture per-request metadata and can stream structured logs to your SIEM. We avoid storing request bodies unless explicitly enabled for debug; by default we do sampling and PII redaction. We'll document retention policies in the security pack.
[00:07:03] Alex: Any blockers around IP allowlist for external partners? We need consistent source IP for partner callbacks.
[00:07:09] Liam: If callbacks go to external partners, you can NAT through your own-managed egress IPs so partner sees your stable IP. If Redwood-managed egress is needed, we can provide static egress via a managed NAT but, again, that requires contractual terms.
[00:07:22] Priya: Ok. I will share our firewall allowlist and a list of partner IP expectations.
[00:07:27] Maya: Great. Quick questions from our side: what is your timeline for production?
[00:07:33] Alex: Ideally Q4 readiness for limited rollout, full roll in Q1. But the POC is a gating factor.
[00:07:39] Maya: Understood. We'll prioritize POC slots accordingly.
[00:07:42] Sam: One more: do you support service account auth and short-lived tokens? We want ephemeral credentials for calls.
[00:07:48] Rina: We support short-lived tokens and mutual TLS option for internal calls. For Private, mTLS to the inference endpoint can be configured.
[00:07:56] Derek: Any legal red flags we should know about? Data residency clauses?
[00:07:59] Maya: Standard terms allow for customer-controlled data residency in Private. We'll route billing metadata to EU on request. Any additional legal language we can push to the next stage with legal.
[00:08:08] Alex: Ok, that's fine.
[00:08:10] Liam: Alright, to recap — action items: we'll send security pack and checklist, propose POC dates, and draft a benchmark plan; you'll send VPC diagram, allowlist needs, and traffic profile.
[00:08:20] Priya: Yep.
[00:08:22] Derek: I have one question on audit retention SLA — can Redwood commit to 2 years retention for audit logs?
[00:08:28] Rina: We can support 2 years retention for logs stored in your S3 or your logging backend; for our control plane logs we usually offer 12 months but we can discuss extended retention as part of the contract.
[00:08:40] Derek: Good to know.
[00:08:42] Maya: Any final questions?
[00:08:44] Alex: None from me. Thanks.
[00:08:46] Sam: No.
[00:08:47] Priya: All good.
[00:08:48] Derek: No.
[00:08:49] Maya: Great — thanks all. We'll follow up with the pack and a calendar invite for POC kickoff.
[00:08:55] Alex: Thanks Maya, Liam.
[00:08:57] (crosstalk)

[00:09:15] -- end of recorded transcript --

Notes on transcription quality: names sometimes misattributed and occasional homophone errors (e.g., "PrivateLink" transcribed as "private link"). Speaker turns are preserved but punctuation may be imperfect.
